idiom_name: struct MonsterType value descriptor + [String: MonsterType] registry; protocols for behaviour
implementation_notes: A struct MonsterType is the natural Swift descriptor: value semantics mean copies cannot alias, Codable conformance decodes the catalogue directly, and the typed object stores it (let type: MonsterType) while keeping its own state. The registry is a [String: MonsterType] dictionary built from decoded JSON; behaviour that varies per type is either data or a protocol existential / closure in the descriptor, which keeps the type set open. Swift's runtime type metadata records and Any.Type describe the compiler's types and cannot carry domain fields, so this is the idiomatic two-declaration form rather than a built-in facility. For a closed set of kinds an enum with associated values plus an exhaustive switch is the compile-checked alternative.
pitfalls: Type descriptors are values: mutating a copy taken from the registry does not change what existing instances hold - replace the entry and construct new instances instead of expecting a shared mutation to propagate.
Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:) traps at runtime on duplicate ids from an unvalidated data file; decode, validate ids, and use the uniquing initializer with an explicit policy.
A closure or class instance inside a struct descriptor reintroduces reference semantics and shared mutable state - keep behaviour stateless or make the sharing explicit.
